provenance.note: transcribed from the author's own text; the model is his, the transcription is this session's

eras.label: Acceleration toward the NHI Crisis
typical_hacking: remote intrusion where a reachable path exists
eras.note: The default setting at new game. Hacker gameplay must not begin as if post-crisis local-only netrunning were already universal. Professional hackers already use BCI, cognitive augmentation, narrow AI and specialist hardware from the start: augmentation and reachability change, the netrunner's capability does not.

eras.label: NHI Crisis
eras.note: The public internet is down or effectively unusable as a strategic global service amid physical destruction, outages, emergency isolation, state and corporate disconnects and hostile AGI incidents. A netrunner may be skilled and still unable to reach a target. Travel and logistics are disrupted too.

eras.label: After the NHI Crisis
typical_hacking: access to a private link or courier
eras.note: A Blackwall-like barrier quarantines the hostile old internet and rogue-AGI digital environments. Safenet is slow and managed, and is NOT a trusted channel for sensitive data. Slow does not equal safe; controlled does not equal confidential.

connectivity_classes.label: public network gateway
connectivity_classes.description: A service reachable over the era's public network while that network is up.
connectivity_classes.note: A public-facing service does not automatically yield privileged network access: access, credentials, separation and defensive response still matter.

connectivity_classes.label: Safenet/Slownet-facing exposure
connectivity_classes.description: An organization's own link to the managed public network, mistakenly open or poorly isolated.
connectivity_classes.note: Maintaining such a bridge is a major information-security failure and yet remains surprisingly common. It is an INFOSEC vulnerability, NOT the same criminal act as bridging the quarantined old internet.

connectivity_classes.label: private point-to-point link
connectivity_classes.description: A dedicated private cable, microwave or optical link between selected sites, with discoverable endpoints and institutional ownership.
connectivity_classes.note: Interceptable and targetable, but not a public route.

connectivity_classes.label: local wired/WLAN only
connectivity_classes.description: A fast, feature-rich local network with no outside route: building WLAN, industrial IoT, local servers, and the Cyber overlay on the physical world.
connectivity_classes.note: A wireless BCI is itself an exposed endpoint on such a network; compromise can threaten its software, attached devices and possibly neural interfaces. Local connectivity is not equivalent to Safenet access, and neither is access to the quarantined old internet.

connectivity_classes.label: isolated / air-gapped
connectivity_classes.description: A system with no connection at all to any network the operator can reach.
connectivity_classes.note: An inaccessible air-gapped machine cannot be hacked remotely by narrative fiat. Reaching it means a physical entry point: a field operation, or a device delivered to the site.

access_paths.label: a netrunner present on site
access_paths.note: The default for serious netrunning, and the only route to a genuinely isolated target.

access_paths.label: a drone or compromised on-site device
access_paths.note: Delivers the local connection where plausible. It still needs a real path back to the operator and can be discovered or jammed, so it works within the locality the era still permits.

access_paths.label: an authorised institutional connection
access_paths.note: A legitimate private link or permission to use one. Requires the authority, not merely the ambition.

access_paths.label: a trusted insider
access_paths.note: A person already inside, cooperating or coerced.

access_paths.label: a compromised courier or media shipment
access_paths.note: Intercepting or altering physically transported storage. It yields the media, not necessarily a live connection.

access_paths.label: a remote attack on a public-facing service
access_paths.note: Requires the era's public network to be up, a genuinely reachable interface, reconnaissance, privileges or exploits, and acceptance of detection risk.

access_paths.label: bridging the quarantined old Internet
access_paths.note: Connecting Safenet or a protected local network to the old Internet. Attempts trigger automated cyberdefense and multinational law-enforcement response, including armed tactical teams.

illegality_classes.label: a mismanaged public-facing exposure
illegality_classes.note: An organization's own carelessness. Serious, recurring, and politically embarrassing, but it is not the criminal act of crossing the containment boundary.

illegality_classes.label: bridging the quarantined old Internet
illegality_classes.note: A grave international crime in every era. These two must never be merged into one 'cyber crime' tag.

refused_as_access_paths.note: A Castellsian social or institutional power relation is not a technical route. Being socially connected to a person does not automatically create a usable network path, and an influence edge on the strategy map is not a TCP connection. These ids are refused by name so the mistake is loud instead of silent.

research_priorities.label: advanced narrow AI without unrestricted autonomous agents
new topologies, verification and post-catastrophe cryptography - no deployed solution has restored trustworthy global secure networking

example_mission.label: obtain data from an on-premises research lab
example_mission.note: One comparable mission across the three periods, as the issue asks. The narrative payoff: a heavily augmented netrunner can become more technologically capable while becoming less globally connected.

periods.route: remote intrusion through a reachable public service, with reconnaissance and an exploit, or a social-engineering entry against staff
the remote route is gone: the operation becomes an expedition - on-site entry, a planted device, or cooperation with someone already inside
periods.what_changes: the same netrunner, the same toolkit, no reachable path

periods.route: a mismanaged Safenet-facing connection, physical presence, a drone or insider, or a private link or courier
periods.what_changes: targets are private LANs and the mistakes that expose them
periods.cost: the containment boundary is now a legal and political hazard as well as a technical one

containment_event.label: a containment breach, a Blackwall political controversy, or a trade-off between security and scientific access
containment_event.note: A world-level event seed, not a scripted outcome. Whose gateway failed, who authorised it, and whether the response is oversight or a crackdown are the political questions the setting's movements fight over.

reconciliation.note: The issue asks that earlier passages stating the internet has already been universally replaced be annotated as describing the post-crisis era. These are the passages found on the default branch; they are listed rather than edited, because the legacy RPG text is not this session's to rewrite (AGENTS.md, and the #306 directive: old lore carries over, do not rewrite the legacy RPG).
